{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-House Counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement (Vendor form)
**Privileged & Confidential — Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The document is, on the whole, unusually favourable to us: the indemnification, intellectual property, assignment/change-of-control, termination-for-convenience, transition assistance, audit, governing law, renewal, insurance, and the absence of exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-commitment and Customer-side MFN provisions all meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline.

Three substantive items require attention, and two of them share a single root cause. The defined term **"Fees"** is drawn narrowly at § 1.5/§ 1.6 to mean only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form. That definition is then used as the measure of (i) Vendor's aggregate liability cap in § 21.1 and (ii) the warranty refund remedy in § 19.4. The practical effect is that Vendor's total exposure — and our only monetary warranty remedy — is pegged near USD 12,000 irrespective of our subscription spend. We treat the liability cap as a critical deviation and the warranty refund as a medium deviation; both are fixed by keying the relevant amounts to all sums paid or payable under the Agreement rather than to the defined "Fees."

Separately, § 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by us of fifteen percent of annual Fees for each week of payment delay. That is punitive in scale and contrary to our position that no liquidated damages or penalties be payable by Customer; we substitute capped simple late-payment interest as Vendor's sole remedy, leaving the ten-day trigger and the § 7.3 dispute-withholding mechanics intact.

Finally, two items are unresolved and require manual attention before we sign off: the licence-grant scope review did not complete, and the non-solicitation finding, while substantively supported by an exhaustive negative search, failed automated verification. Neither is currently believed to be a problem, but neither is cleared.

---

## 2. Findings Table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability | Cap is mutual and carve-outs match playbook, but the basis is illusory: "Fees" = USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, and § 21.1 further narrows to the first Order Form. No USD 1,000,000 floor. |
| 2 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification | Unqualified Vendor IP defence/indemnity (20.1) extended to Affiliates; misconduct limbs at 20.2 meet and in part exceed our model; standard procedure at 20.4; procure/modify/replace/refund remedies at 20.5 are additive. Customer's reciprocal indemnity at 20.3 is appropriately narrow. Excluded Claims confirmed at 21.3. |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables | Customer owns Customer Data and Deliverables with express assignment (14.1–14.2); Vendor retains only Vendor Technology, with the § 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence for embedded material; joint ownership barred (14.4). No aggregated/de-identified data carve-out. |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes | § 7.7 imposes liquidated damages on Customer of 15% of annual Fees per week of delay — punitive and contrary to our no-LD position. No early-termination fee elsewhere (§ 9.4 limits us to accrued Fees). |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Needs review** | — | Automated review did not complete (tool loop exceeded 12 iterations). Requires manual review; no conclusion reached. |
| 6 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control | Consent-free Customer assignment to Affiliate/successor (24.1); Vendor assignment and change-of-control transfer gated by our consent and never to a competitor (24.2); § 24.4 denies Vendor any repricing, acceleration or termination on our change of control. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | No exclusivity, sole-supplier or all-requirements obligation. § 12.3 preserves our freedom to source elsewhere; § 2.1 confirms no purchase commitment. § 12.4 exclusivity-type restraint runs against Vendor and is to be retained. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | No covenant restricts our businesses, products, fields or territories; § 12.3 confirms the opposite. Competition restraints at 12.4 and § 24 run against Vendor. § 13.4 limits are ordinary anti-reverse-engineering terms. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination | § 9.4 gives us without-cause termination of the Agreement or any Order Form on 30 days' notice (via § 29.4), exposure limited to accrued Fees, with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees. No early-termination fee. Vendor has no convenience exit during the § 8.1 three-year term. |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 19 Warranties | Warranty scope and ladder are strong, but the § 19.4 refund of "Fees paid for it" is capped by definition at the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee and can never return subscription fees — the amounts actually at risk under the § 19.2 full-term Hosted Services warranty. |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | **Needs review** | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | Exhaustive search found no non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binding Customer, and § 12.3 preserves our right to hire responders to general recruitment. Substantively our preferred position, but automated verification failed — confirm manually. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor's cost unless >5% underpayment; no direct system access; findings are our Confidential Information. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution | New York law with CISG disclaimed; exclusive jurisdiction in New York County state and federal courts. No arbitration provision. Injunctive-relief carve-out and executive escalation are mutual. |
| 14 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes | The only MFN (§ 7.6) runs in our favour. No Customer-side MFN; § 12.3 confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment. |
| 15 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope | § 2.1 disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment; § 7.1 bars undisclosed minimum-use charges; § 12.3 confirms no minimum-volume commitment. § 22 "shortfall" references concern Vendor underpayment true-ups only. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal | 12-month renewals; Customer-only opt-out on 30 days' notice; Vendor reminder 60 days out with deadline extension if missed; § 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3%. The § 8.1 three-year commitment is an initial term, not a multi-year auto-renewal. |
| 17 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return | Up to six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates (11.1); data return within 30 days in machine-readable format with no withholding for fee disputes (11.2); deletion only after our confirmation, with officer certification (11.3). |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance | CGL USD 1M/2M, workers' comp plus employer's liability USD 1M, professional E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, term plus one year; certificates on request; insurance expressly does not limit Vendor's liabilities. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

We identify one item as non-negotiable in its current form:

- **§ 21.1 — Illusory liability cap (Critical).** A cap measured by the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form gives Vendor effectively no exposure for the subscription services we are buying. The mutuality and Excluded Claims architecture in § 21.3 is sound and we will preserve it, but the cap basis must be re-keyed to all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor. We should not sign on the current basis.

No other finding rises to walk-away status. The § 7.7 liquidated damages and the § 19.4 refund basis are firm asks but are capable of resolution through the redlines described below. No walk-away parameter is triggered by the § 8.1 three-year initial term, which is an initial commitment rather than a multi-year automatic renewal.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. **Issue the § 21.1 redline (Critical).** Tie the cap to all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor, leaving mutuality and the § 21.3 Excluded Claims list untouched. Position this to Vendor as a correction of a definitional artefact rather than a reallocation of risk.
2. **Issue the § 7.7 redline (High).** Delete the fifteen-percent-per-week liquidated damages and substitute simple interest capped at one percent per month, or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law (§ 1.2), as Vendor's sole remedy. Preserve the existing ten-day trigger and the § 7.3 dispute-withholding mechanics. No fallback cap on early-termination fees is required, as none exists.
3. **Issue the § 19.4 redline (Medium).** Scope the refund to all amounts paid for the affected item, including prepaid subscription and other charges, and expressly not limited to the Implementation Fee. Express the Deliverable warranty period as "ninety (90) days" for clarity — a conforming edit only, not a change of term. Leave the re-perform/repair/replace ladder and the non-exclusivity carve-outs untouched.
4. **Complete the licence-grant scope review (High).** The automated review of the LICENSE rule did not finish and reached no conclusion. Assign this for manual review of the § 13 grant language before we clear the document.
5. **Confirm the non-solicitation finding (Medium).** The negative search is thorough and § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our hiring freedom, but automated verification failed. Have a reviewer confirm the absence of any Customer-side non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant. If Vendor later proposes adding one, our fallback is a mutual covenant limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, twelve months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
6. **Consider a definitional fix.** Because the narrow "Fees" definition at § 1.5/§ 1.6 drives both the § 21.1 and § 19.4 defects, we may propose amending the definition itself as an alternative to the two clause-level edits. We recommend leading with the clause-level redlines and holding the definitional approach in reserve.
7. **Do not spend capital on:** the narrowing of the malicious-code warranty to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor" (§ 19.3), which we regard as customary and not worth negotiating at medium severity; and the Vendor-favouring restraints at § 12.4, § 24 and § 7.6, which benefit us and should be retained as drafted."}
